Hello ggplot2 users,

First of all I would like to apologise because I’m very new to R and
therefore also to the package ggplot2; I’m writing to this forum
because I hope to find here some help for a definitive and neat way to
deal with my sort of personal “chart puzzle”.
I’ve been trying various solutions with so many different softwares
but none of them was plainly satisfactory to me.
In very short what I would like to do with R is the following type of
chart: https://sites.google.com/site/wantedchart/

a scatter plot with both x and y axes set in logarithmic scale, points
plotted with x and y error bars, leading lines to legend points to be
positioned at given specific positions in the chart frame (in order to
avoid label overlapping)

Can anyone please give me some “boostraping hints” from where and how
is better to start with?
Yes, I know I should have posted this message after a careful reading
of available documentation but I’m really somehow lost in the middle
of the forest of the R commands; I’m not looking for a pre-cooked
solution for my problem but rather an indication of the right path to
follow…

So far I’ve done a very much basic scatter plot without any useful
control on axis scales and most of all on the plotting of the error
bars and the point legends and the corresponding leading lines….again,
in short I’m hopeless!

Thank you very much for any help

maxbre

Seems like we just had our wires crossed thanks to some gmail timewarping. 

You should be really close now though. You can do the calculation in the geom_errorbar() and geom_errorbarh() calls. See their help pages for details. http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/

A bit more tweaking of the sizes and you're mostly there. The only thing that isn't nice is the justification. You should be able to supply a vector of justifications, one for each label in the order of the levels. hjust = 0 for labels on the right and hjust = 1 for labels on the left. At least I think you can do this. 

I sure hope you're making more than one of these... 

B
